This confirms the full picture. Sweep results:

**17 call sites** across 7 files still pass the legacy `legacyRounding` second argument:

| File | Count |
|---|---|
| `src\reports\quarterly.js` | 5 (`bundle`, `holdback`, `subtotal`, `surcharge`, `gross`) |
| `src\billing\invoice.js` | 3 (`tip`, `balance`, `payout`) |
| `src\admin\exports.js` | 3 (`tip`, `commission`, `credit`) |
| `src\checkout\cart.js` | 2 (`prepayment`, `writeOff`) |
| `src\reports\monthly.js` | 2 (`tip`, `settlement`) |
| `src\billing\statement.js` | 1 (`bundle`) |
| `src\checkout\receipt.js` | 1 (`tip`) |

**`src\reports\quarterly.js` has the most**, with 5 two-argument calls (all pass `true`). The definition lives in `src\lib\format.js:6` (`function formatAmount(value, legacyRounding)`) — worth noting `src\reports\ledger.js`, `src\admin\dashboard.js`, and `src\billing\refunds.js` are already clean, single-arg only.
